questions.stem: Reflect the point (3, 4) across the line y = x. Which of the following is the correct reflected point?
questions.solution: The reflection across the line y = x swaps the x and y coordinates of a point. So, if we start with (3, 4), the reflected point will have its x-coordinate as the original y-coordinate and vice versa: (4, 3).
questions.explanation: Reflection across the line y = x is a common transformation in geometry that swaps the x and y values of each coordinate.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake would be to choose option B, which reflects the point along the x-axis instead of the line y = x. Remember that reflection across y = x only swaps coordinates.

questions.stem: Reflect the triangle with vertices A(1, 2), B(3, 4), and C(5, 6) across the line y = x. Which of the following is the correct reflected point for vertex B?
questions.solution: Reflecting vertex B(3, 4) across the line y = x will swap its coordinates: (4, 3).
questions.explanation: Reflecting a shape across a line involves reflecting each of its vertices. The same rule for individual points applies.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake would be to choose option B, which reflects the point along the y-axis instead of the line y = x. Remember that reflection across y = x only swaps coordinates.

questions.stem: Reflect the equation y = 2x + 1 across the line y = x. Which of the following is the correct reflected equation?
questions.solution: Reflecting the equation across y = x means swapping x and y. So, y becomes x and vice versa: x = 2y + 1.
questions.explanation: When reflecting an equation, treat it as a point (slope-intercept form) or line and apply the reflection rule accordingly.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake would be to choose option C, which reflects the slope incorrectly. Remember that the slope changes sign when reflecting across y = x.

questions.stem: Reflect the parabola defined by the equation y = (x - 2)^2 + 3 across the line y = x. Which of the following is the correct reflected equation?
questions.solution: Reflecting the parabola across y = x means swapping x and y: x = (y - 2)^2 + 3.
questions.explanation: When reflecting a more complex function, like a parabola, apply the reflection rule to each term in the equation.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake would be to choose option C, which reflects the vertex incorrectly. Remember that only the x and y values change; the structure of the equation remains the same.

questions.stem: Reflect the circle with center (3, 4) and radius 2 across the line y = x. Which of the following is the correct reflected circle's center?
questions.solution: Reflecting the circle across y = x swaps the coordinates of its center: (4, 3). The radius remains unchanged.
questions.explanation: Reflecting a circle involves reflecting its center point and keeping the radius constant.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake would be to choose option B, which reflects the circle along the x-axis instead of the line y = x. Remember that reflection across y = x only swaps coordinates.

questions.stem: Reflect the function f(x) = 3sin(x) + 2 across the line y = x. Which of the following is the correct reflected function?
questions.solution: Reflecting the function across y = x means swapping x and y: x = 3sin(y) + 2.
questions.explanation: When reflecting a function, treat it as a set of points and apply the reflection rule accordingly.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake would be to choose option C, which reflects the function's coefficients incorrectly. Remember that only the x and y values change; the structure of the function remains the same.

questions.stem: Reflect the line segment connecting points A(-1, 2) and B(4, 5) across the line y = x. Which of the following is the correct reflected point for B?
questions.solution: Reflecting point B(4, 5) across y = x swaps its coordinates: (5, 4).
questions.explanation: Reflecting a line segment involves reflecting each endpoint and keeping the line connecting them.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake would be to choose option C, which reflects the point along the x-axis instead of the line y = x. Remember that reflection across y = x only swaps coordinates.
